title: Multi-Object Detection Through Meta-Training in Resource-Constrained UAV-Based Surveillance Applications
problem: Object detection in UAV surveillance requires real-time performance on resource-constrained edge devices. Domain variation (nighttime, crowds, weather, small objects) degrades detection accuracy, and standard models trained on limited domains generalize poorly to real-world conditions.
motivation: UAV-based surveillance operates across diverse environmental and lighting conditions. Generalizing YOLO models across domains without retraining on each condition improves practical deployability. Meta-training enables transfer learning across diverse domains, improving robustness with minimal overhead.
method: Meta-training framework for domain generalization (adaptation): YOLO models trained iteratively across diverse domains (nighttime, crowds, sunny weather, small objects) using gradient descent-based optimization. Transfer learning enables model to learn domain-adaptive features. Multiple YOLO configurations and public/custom datasets tested.
key_novelty: Meta-training approach for domain generalization in YOLO-based object detection; demonstrates improved generalization across environmental adversities in UAV surveillance without single-domain overfitting.
contributions: Meta-training framework for domain generalization in YOLO models
Improved multi-domain generalization across nighttime, crowd, weather, and small object detection
Average precision (AP) improvements demonstrated on custom and public drone datasets
Deployment validation on three commercially available resource-constrained devices

metrics.secondary: generalization improvement (quantitative value not specified in abstract)

limitations: Abstract only; specific AP improvements not quantified; resource-constrained device specs (CPU, memory, FLOPs) not specified; comparison with other domain adaptation methods missing; training time and convergence analysis not provided; specific meta-training algorithm details not disclosed; performance vs. accuracy tradeoffs not characterized; scalability to more domains not discussed.
